sections.title: Intuition is for everyone, so why is this page created specifically for athletes?

blocks.body: Because I believe that intuition is essential in sport.

Throughout their careers, athletes often experience a powerful connection to their intuition. At least once, every competitive athlete has experienced moments when they instinctively know something that goes beyond the logical next step, their coach’s instructions or an agreed strategy.

blocks.text: The momentum, instinct, feel for the game — whatever you call it.

blocks.body: They bring an immediate sense of flow and clarity — an inner shift that changes the outer reality.
How long and deep this connection goes often determines an athlete’s ability to turn a difficult situation in their favour, stay present and creative, and enjoy their performance.

blocks.text:
You can only control yourself.
The rest is out of your control.

blocks.alt: Close-up portrait: part of a woman’s face, looking at the camera

blocks.body: A space to develop the ability to connect with yourself, listen to your inner voice and recognise what it is saying.

blocks.heading: Intuition speaks differently to everyone
blocks.body: For some, intuition comes as a gut feeling or a sensation in the heart; for others, as a voice, an image, a sudden flash of insight, or even something that appears in a dream. Sometimes it arrives instantly and clearly; at other times it is subtle and needs silence, patience and attention to notice.

blocks.text: Not everything in life can be understood through logic, nor does everything need to be.

blocks.heading: Where we begin
blocks.body: Our work begins with exploring what intuition means to you: how you naturally perceive it, how it shows up in different situations, and what helps you recognise its signals. You learn to notice, distinguish and interpret these messages, while developing the confidence to trust your own perceptions.

blocks.text: As with any new experience, curiosity, courage, openness and trust are essential. Above all, bring a willingness to explore, to experience something new, and to discover your beautiful self.

blocks.body: Intuition can reconnect us with our inner truth: our values, what makes us happy, what we want from life and how we wish to move through it. Yet this journey is not only about understanding and answers. It is also about learning to accept the unknown, the unpredictable and the uncontrollable. Letting go of the boundaries that stand in the way of your inner alignment and contentment is one of the few skills we practise.

blocks.heading: How the sessions work
blocks.body:
These sessions are led intuitively and individually. There is no predefined programme designed for everyone. My approach is not based on scientific studies or established concepts, but neither does it seek to deny or exclude any particular perspective.

It is not psychological counselling or conventional mental training, though we may touch on some elements of those methods. Sessions normally unfold naturally, instinctively: your intuition will lead us to where your attention and awareness are most needed.

blocks.title: What we can explore together
blocks.intro: Connecting to intuition on a deeper level can help athletes navigate both sport and life with greater awareness, balance and self-trust. These are a few examples of what we might explore.
blocks.d1: Staying connected to the process rather than fixating on the result.
blocks.d2: Telling it apart from fears, mental chatter and external expectations.
blocks.d3: Building a deeper relationship with it, and learning to notice what it is telling you.
blocks.d4: Accepting periods of uncertainty, crisis, rest, growth and change as natural parts of everyone’s path.
blocks.d5: Expressing yourself beyond social pressure and rigid ideas of what is right or wrong, possible or impossible.
blocks.d6: Shifting attention and energy towards other meaningful aspects of life, and developing an identity beyond sport.
blocks.finalText: Checking with yourself before and after listening to the advice of family, friends, coaches, doctors and other experts. No one knows whats right for you better than you.

blocks.text: Transformation isn’t a call to change your outer circumstances. Its an inner journey towards wholeness.

blocks.heading: Transformation is not an easy period but it has a rewarding results
blocks.body:
It often begins independently of our readiness or desire. At a certain point in life, we feel that something is changing — first inside us.

Initially, we dismiss these shifts, calling them moods or temporary phases, thinking that once something external changes, we’ll return to normal.
But at some point, we realise this is not something that will simply pass. We can’t run from it or keep denying it.

blocks.text: The first step is to acknowledge the truth: we are changing.

blocks.body: You recognise this stage when things that once mattered lose their power — what used to bring you joy, purpose and satisfaction no longer does. There is a sense of inner confusion, a void where nothing feels alive or purposeful.

We reach for what is familiar: it feels safe, even when it no longer fits. Resisting change is natural — we do not know what lies on the other side.

This discomfort is hard to endure for long. Some manage, but often the easiest path is to face it — to welcome what is emerging, to embrace the transformation.

blocks.heading: Rediscovering what feels like you
blocks.body: After years of parental advice, education and social conditioning, we often drift far from who we truly are. Transformation pushes us to step back and rediscover what truly feels like us.

In this stage there is a lot of social pressure. People offer well-meaning advice — just keep trying, see a therapist, change jobs, find a new relationship. These shifts might distract you, but ultimately you might confront the same inner truths again.

This can lead to social alienation and feeling of loosing touch with your life.

blocks.heading: How I can support here
blocks.body:
What I offer is simply to be a witness — a steady presence as you navigate these shifts, to normalise and name what you’re feeling. Let yourself relax in unknown and uncomfortable. 
This is deep and individual work, but everyone sometimes needs a hand to hold in these moments. Of course, it’s not a hand you rely on forever. Much of the journey you walk alone, but a witness — someone who can name your experience as valid and normal — can make the difference.

I speak from my own journey, and what I offer is to be that hand, that witness, perhaps even that guide, whenever you need it.

blocks.text: If you are walking this path and don’t have that support, you can reach out.

blocks.body: Although I am not an athlete myself, sport has always been part of my life.

From joining grassroots sports clubs as a child to becoming a passionate sports fan and eventually working as a Competition Manager at one of the world’s largest sports organisations, my journey has taken me through many different sides of sport.

During my ten years at FIFA, I contributed to the organisation of football World Cups, as well as numerous related events. Along the way, I met athletes at different stages of their careers, each with their own backgrounds, experiences, ambitions, and challenges. Through these encounters, I gradually developed a deeper interest in the person behind the athlete — their individual journey, their inner world, and the challenges that may remain unseen from the outside.

blocks.text: Over time, I began to envision a space where athletes could find support beyond their sporting achievements.

blocks.body:
A few years ago, my own life took a turn that had been brewing within me for some time. I left a successful career without knowing what would come next. This gave me space to pause and look inward, to reflect on who I really am and what I want. I delved into psychology, body and energy practices, alternative healing approaches, and ancient philosophies. I explored my own perceptions and senses, experimented, and gradually discovered new ways of understanding myself and, most importantly, enjoying my life.

I have always been intuitive, even as a child. Unfortunately, my sensitivity was often dismissed or not taken seriously by my family, so I never learned to trust it. Over the past few years, however, I have managed to find my own voice beneath layers of family conditioning and social expectations. I have learned to trust myself more deeply and rely less on external validation or the need for constant control and security. This journey continues to this day.
Today, through the individual sessions I offer, I am bringing this idea of creating a supportive space for athletes to life.

blocks.text: Guiding others in their search for self-trust, fulfilment, and happiness has become a meaningful part of my own journey, too.
